key_insight: Chronicle is an explainable transformer that learns from full patient treatment timelines to continuously predict cancer risks across many cancer types and healthcare systems.
clinical_relevance: It could help clinicians update prognostic estimates over time using routine hospital data, supporting more personalized treatment planning and monitoring.
method: Trained on 53.7 million longitudinal data points from 51,711 patients across 67 cancer types
Uses irregular, real-world timelines directly without imputation
Jointly predicts eight clinical endpoints with built-in explainability
evidence_signal: In the abstract, Chronicle outperformed cross-sectional survival models (C-index 0.84 vs 0.76-0.79), predicted seven adverse outcomes with AUC 0.80-0.92, and generalized to 69,341 patients across Germany, Switzerland, and the United States.
watch_item: Real-world deployment may still require local fine-tuning, careful validation across sites, and workflow integration to ensure reliable performance.
paper_title: An explainable transformer model learning from entire treatment timelines for pan-cancer risk profiling across healthcare systems
